title: Fair Process for Termination Due to Poor Performance and Recourse for Employees
what_it_is: Fair Process for Termination Due to Poor Performance and Recourse for Employees

sections.label: Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment
sections.summary: The Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices require employers terminating employees for poor performance to apply relevant and objective performance criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices make it clear that employers who wish to terminate the services of employees on the ground of poor performance are to apply relevant and objective performance criteria.

sections.label: Surbana Jurong termination and ex-gratia payment
sections.summary: Employers unable to substantiate poor performance claims may be ordered to reinstate or compensate; Surbana Jurong acknowledged its process could have been better managed and agreed on ex-gratia payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: If an employer is unable to substantiate his claim that the employee's performance is poor, the employer may be ordered to reinstate the employee or to provide compensation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In the case of Surbana Jurong's recent exercise to terminate the services of 54 employees, the company has acknowledged that the process could have been better managed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The management and unions have since reached an agreement on an ex-gratia payment which, in our view, is a fair outcome for the affected employees.

sections.label: Manpower Minister on labelling poor performers
sections.summary: The Manpower Minister recalls this as the first major termination exercise where an employer publicly labelled workers as poor performers, which he does not find acceptable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: To the best of my recollection, this is the first time that an employer has conducted such a major termination exercise and to declare publicly and to label the workers as poor performers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: This is something that, as the Manpower Minister, I do not find acceptable.

sections.label: Responsible and sensitive performance management
sections.summary: The management publicly acknowledged the exercise could have been better managed, and the Minister hopes to make clear that employers should do performance management responsibly and sensitively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The management realises this as well and that is why they publicly acknowledged that the way they conducted the exercise could have been much better managed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: I hope to make clear to all employers out there that when it comes to performance management, do it responsibly and, at the same time, do it sensitively.
